text:
lia: spinning up Atlas-6B (int4) today. smoke passed until ~120-140 tokens, then outputs slowly drift vs fp16 baseline. looks like a rotary packing + tokenizer normalizer double-run got tangled in the exporter.

anna: double-run normalizer? like casefold applied twice so token ids near punctuation changed? paste token ids near drift.

sam: also check quant scales per-head. we saw a case where headwise scale rounding plus odd rotary packing produced phase-slip after warmup. :mag:

lia: quick repro: run fp16 then int4, compare topk at step=130. tail ids: [1, 345, 58, 902, 30522, 9, 3] — note 30522 in there which is a high-valued sentinel in some exports. model.json shows: "rotary_pack": "zigzag", "rotary_dim":64, "n_heads":16, "token_normalizer_passes":2, "vocab_map_overlay": true

kevin: zigzag is a vendor-specific packing (e.g., [0,12,1,13,2,14,3,15,4,8,5,9,6,10,7,11]) — if loader assumes contiguous heads that misindexes KV cache. double normalizer could shift tokenization boundaries too. Combined, they explain gradual drift.

raj: run `export-inspect atlas.bin --rotary-map` and `tok-inspect --detect-double-normalize atlas.json` and paste outputs.

lia: inspector outputs: `rotary_map: [0,12,1,13,2,14,3,15,4,8,5,9,6,10,7,11]` and tokenizer check: `normalizer_passes:2, casefold_applied:true` plus `vocab_overlay_table: {50260:30522}`. Our tokenizer only runs one pass and expects no overlay.

sam: that exact zigzag map will create a uneven phase distribution; combined with per-head quant scale off-by-one rounding we can get slow logit drift. Two fixes: remap heads at load-time and normalize token ids by reversing overlay; also verify per-head quant scales against fp16 activations.

anna: add an activation sanity: compute mean abs diff for first 8 tokens post-remap between fp16 and int4 < 1e-3. For tokenizer, apply reverse overlay before generation so downstream sees canonical ids. Also add a small test to detect double normalization by running roundtrip encode->decode and asserting idempotence.

kevin: caution: some vendors also reorder projection groups (qkv vs kvq). When remapping, assert q/k/v grouping expected. Add sample elementwise comparison for a few elements to detect qkv mismatches.

ci-bot: CI: atlas-int4-smoke failed: ppl delta +0.25 at 04:02:01. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/2788

lia: plan: 1) load-time zigzag remap using rotary_map, 2) reverse vocab_overlay at tokenizer boundary, 3) add double-normalize detector and warn/fail if exporter did weirdness, 4) add unit tests: top-1 equality for first 160 tokens and tokenizer roundtrip idempotence, 5) activation L2 check. ETA WIP PR later today.

sam: also add a nightly regression job that runs ngram-overlap on our helpfulness set for newly onboarded models so subtle quality deltas show up.

raj: emit telemetry when auto-remap or overlay reverse applied so we can contact vendor. Recommend vendor canonicalization: single normalizer pass, head-major rotary, no vocab overlays.

lia: pushing WIP PR with inspector commands, remap snippet, tokenizer reverse map, and CI link. will ping once green. :white_check_mark:
